name: load_macro_from_url

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: `https://` URL whose response body is one SQL [`CREATE MACRO`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/statements/create_macro) statement (scalar or table macro). Redirects are followed, and each hop is checked again; any non-`200` response raises an error. On DuckDB 2.0, plain `http://` is refused unless `SET webmacro_allow_http = true`.

description:
Fetch the URL, check that the response body is a macro definition, create the macro, and return `Successfully loaded macro: <name>`. The macro is then callable by name like any other DuckDB macro.

The response body must be exactly one `CREATE MACRO` or `CREATE OR REPLACE MACRO` statement. Anything else raises an error and nothing runs, including a macro followed by another statement. The check covers what runs when the file loads, not what the macro does when you call it, so the security model is **trust the URL**. See the Trust model section.

**DuckDB 2.0 build:** the request goes through DuckDB's HTTP stack (httpfs is autoloaded for `https://`), so `http_timeout`, `http_retries`, `http_proxy` and HTTP secrets apply. Plain `http://` is refused unless `webmacro_allow_http` is set, responses over `webmacro_max_response_size` bytes (default 1 MiB) are refused, and the function refuses to run when `enable_external_access` is false. The macro is created in your own transaction and search path, so `TEMP` macros work and a `ROLLBACK` removes the macro. The function is `VOLATILE`. The Haybarn 1.5 build still creates the macro on a separate connection and rejects `TEMP` macros.
